CORAM:
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE YOGESH KHANNA  ORDER % 15.02.2023 1.

Petitioners file this writ petition for quashing of the FIR No.525/2016 under Section 406/498A/34 Indian Penal Code and Section 4 of the D.P. Act registered at police station S.B.Dairy,
Delhi against them and the proceedings emanating therefrom.
2. The marriage between the petitioner No.1 and complainant/ respondent No.2 was solemnized on 10.10.2015 according to Muslim rites and ceremonies at Delhi.
One son was born from the wedlock.

However, due to matrimonial discord, the petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 separated and on the complaint of respondent No.2 in CAW Cell, Rohini, Delhi, the present FIR was registered against the petitioners.
Charghesheet has since been filed in the year 2017.
3. On 06.04.2022 the matter was amicably settled between the parties and the said MoU/Settlement is on record as Annexure A-4.
As per the Settlement the petitioner No.1 was to pay Rs.5.30 lacs including Rs.50,000/- for the son viz. Ahill.
Such FDR of Rs.50,000/- has since been handed over to the respondent No.2.
Today balance of Rs.2.80 lacs has been paid to respondent No.2 vide DD dated 07.02.2023 bearing No.502464 drawn on Bank of Baroda in favour of respondent No.2.

sentences.text: The parties have also obtained divorce/Talaq on mutual consent under Muslim Law.

5. The complainant/respondent No.2 has been duly identified by the Investigating Officer and states the matter has been settled and she has no objection if the FIR is quashed against the petitioners and she has received entire amount of Rs.4.80 lacs towards all her claims of alimony, maintenance - past, present and future, stridhan, and dowry articles etc.
The affidavits of parties are on record.
6. The learned ASC for the State has also no objection, if this petition is allowed.

7. Considering the above settlement between the parties, there is no impediment in quashing of the FIR as complainant has settled all the disputes and has received the settled amount from the petitioners.
In view of the above, there is no use to continue with the proceedings against petitioners as it would never entail in conviction of petitioners.
8. It is made clear this settlement would not come in the way in case the child may like to exercise his right against the father in future.
9. Accordingly, the petition is allowed.
Consequently, FIR No.525/2016 under Section 406/498A/34 Indian Penal Code registered at police station S.B.Dairy, Delhi and the proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
Pending application, if any, also stands disposed of.

YOGESH KHANNA, J.
